text:
cody-cs: Orchid onboarding blocked — their serverless warmup is getting a flood of 429s on SDK init. Cutover tomorrow, they need a quick unblock.
cody-cs: Paste from their Cloud Function logs: 
```
POST https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/init
Headers: { Authorization: Bearer <ephemeral>, User-Agent: OrchidFn/1.0 }
Response: 429 {\"error\": \"rate_limit\", \"retry_after\": 2 }
```
yuki-cs: They report spinning ~40 serverless instances during CI warmup (parallel cold starts). Also seeing sporadic 401s when ephemeral tokens rotate concurrently.
liam-eng: Likely pattern: massive cold-start fanout + synchronized token refresh -> tenant bucket exhausted quickly. Serverless makes this worse because instances don't share a warm cache. Ask for tenant id and traceroute IPs.
cody-cs: Tenant id = t-orchid-77. Traceroute IPs: 203.0.113.12, 34.86.7.191, 35.204.4.10.
infra-bot: anomaly detected: tenant=t-orchid-77 spike at 2026-06-05T11:12:01Z _ concurrent_inits=42 _ token_rotate_window=6s.
dev-rel: Customer-side immediate mitigations: 1) apply client-side connection reuse / keepalive where possible, 2) set explicit region/edge on init, 3) cap preflight/init concurrency in SDK, 4) add jitter to token refresh (spread rotations). Provide a python snippet.
serverless-se: For serverless we recommend a tiny init shim to serialize first-run token refreshes per-deployment or use a lightweight warm pool of 3 steady functions to amortize ephemerals.
liam-eng: Service-side short-term fixes: A) temporary tenant rate cap bump for preflight/init, B) enable header-based edge fallback (X-Redwood-Region) for preflight, C) add a small per-tenant burst window in the rate limiter to absorb short warmups. Ops sign-off required for A/C.
_dev-rel: Python snippet to send them: 
```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(
    api_key='__ephemeral__',
    region='eu-west-1',
    preflight_max_concurrency=3,
    auth_refresh_jitter_ms=300,
    http_keepalive=True
)
# In serverless coldstart, add a tiny sleep jitter before refresh
import time, random
time.sleep(random.uniform(0.05, 0.35))
client.init()
```
liam-eng: Note: http_keepalive reduces TCP+TLS handshake fanout on cold starts and helps edge routing stability. If they can reuse a warm helper instance across cold-starts, that also reduces preflight calls.
yuki-cs: Customer agreed to try SDK shim + reduce warmup parallelism from 40->6 and add the jitter. They also accepted a temporary ops bump if needed.
ops: Please file a ticket for temporary cap bump and routing exception for t-orchid-77. Include IPs and time window.
infra-bot: ticket INC-10021 created: request temporary preflight/init cap bump for t-orchid-77 to 80 for 12h and route listed IPs to eu-west pool. Tagged infra+edge.
liam-eng: I'll canary a small change to the preflight rate limiter to allow a short burst window for preflight/init endpoints for tenants with recent onboarding flags (low-risk).
dev-rel: Also recommend upgrading to python-sdk v0.10.0 which contains serverless warmup guidance and default jittered refresh.
yuki-cs: I'll send the python snippet + warmup playbook to Orchid and ask them to run a 10-min smoke test after applying changes.
ops: INC-10021 approved and temporary cap bump applied until 2026-06-06T00:00:00Z. Monitoring enabled for t-orchid-77.
cody-cs: Thanks everyone. I'll follow up tomorrow after the cutover and post a short onboarding note about serverless-specific warmup best practices (keepalive, jitter, warm helper). :thumbsup:
